title: What Happens to a House After the Founder?
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: A house survives its founder only if the organization can distinguish what must continue, what may evolve, who may decide, which obligations remain, and what evidence authorizes each answer.
Evening dress is retained as evidence, education, reporting or rights context.
narrativeSequence.rights: Object record marks image Public Domain under Met Open Access; retain title, maker, date, accession, credit, and canonical link.

narrativeSequence.caption: 01 · STABILIZE — What cannot wait?. Secure people, payroll, orders, client commitments, facilities, insurance, accounts, credentials, physical objects, master files, and communications. Do not make permanent symbolic decisions inside the first emergency response.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · LOCATE — Where does authority reside?. Map board and officer authority, ownership, employment, IP, licenses, estate or probate instruments, archive agreements, and operational delegations by jurisdiction and record.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · INTERPRET — What should continue—and why?. Separate non-negotiable values, teachable method, recurring codes, historical accidents, commercial habits, and motifs. Preserve the decision logic, not a taxidermy of the last collection.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · ACCOUNT — Who may test the next chapter?. Define successor scope, review bodies, worker and collaborator credit, community consultation, archive citation, performance measures, correction, and removal or renewal.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

mapping.prompt: Run a 72-hour founder-absence simulation across people, money, orders, facilities, accounts, rights, archive, and public communication.
Attach the governing record and backup decision-maker to every critical action.
Sort house codes into values, methods, motifs, habits, and unresolved contradictions.
Prepare continue, pause, license, sell, donate, and close scenarios with qualified counsel, tax, employment, conservation, and cultural advisers.
